QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_13

question.text: Which personal-trading policy control is MOST directly aimed at preventing 'front-running' by Investment Manager employees at a Cat III AIF?

answer.text: Mandatory pre-clearance of employee personal trades and blackout windows around the fund's trading orders
Annual trustee performance review of the AMC

explanation.text: The Logic: Front-running is where an employee trades ahead of the fund's known orders for personal benefit. Pre-clearance by compliance plus a blackout window (e.g., 7 days before/after fund trades in the same security) is the direct control. The Code of Conduct (clauses g, j, k) further reinforces no inducement and confidentiality. The Trap: The other options are legitimate governance items but don't directly address front-running, which requires person-level trading surveillance. Cross-Exam Context: Same concept in XV (Research Analyst — personal trading), XXI-B (PMS), and III-A (Compliance). XIX-E applies in a hedge-fund long-short desk where front-running is highest-risk. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a Cat III long-short fund, require all KMPs and PMs to use a single broker account with read-only trade feeds auto-routed to compliance; deny proprietary shorting in the fund's trade universe. This closes the loophole where an employee shorts a stock hours before the fund unwinds a long.
